newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up, led by Sindicato Antioqueno.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up, led by Sindicato Antioqueno.

text.p: Colombian stocks gained Monday led by shares of the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate.
Bogota's IBB index ended up 0.69 percent at 1,180.78 on trading of 16.3 billion peso, while Medellin's IBOMED closed up 0.68 percent at 17,759.14. The trading volume for Medellin was not available.

"The market was driven by shares in the companies that make up the Sindicato Antioqueno. There was interest from foreign funds, as well as cross deals by existing shareholders," one Bogota broker said.

One of the day's biggest gains was insurance company Suramericana de Seguros, flagship of the Sindicato. Its shares closed up 4.34 percent at 28,800 on volume of 3.1 billion pesos in Bogota and up 5.45 percent at 29,000 on 211 million pesos in Medellin.
Last week, the banking superintendency reported that Suramericana's first-quarter net profits were up 161 percent to 60.9 billion pesos, compared with the same period in 1996.
Cementos del Caribe, also part of the Sindicato, closed up 1.23 percent at 5,720 in Bogota and up 0.52 percent at the same price in Medellin.
The bulk of the volume in Bogota was made up by a nine billion pesos pocket-to-pocket cross deal in cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco, also part of the Sindicato. It closed unchanged at 3,500.
Banco de Bogota, flagship of Luis Carlos Sarmiento's financial empire, closed up 1.76 percent at 6,875 on the Bogota exchange.
